what_it_is.prose: AI Engineering Services Limited (AIESL) — formerly Air India Engineering Services Limited — is the largest aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) organisation in India. It was the engineering and maintenance arm of the state carrier Air India and, when Air India was privatised and sold to the Tata Group, AIESL was carved out and retained by the Government of India, remaining a wholly government-owned public-sector undertaking under the Ministry of Civil Aviation (with residual holding via the Air India Assets Holding structure). Headquartered at the Safdarjung Airport Complex in New Delhi, AIESL provides base (heavy) checks, engine overhaul, component overhaul, landing-gear servicing, wheels-and-brakes overhaul, non-destructive testing, battery services and automatic test-equipment support. It operates narrow- and wide-body hangars at New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Nagpur and Trivandrum, plus more than 50 line stations across the country, and holds 16 approvals from the FAA, EASA and India's DGCA. Its capability set covers Airbus A320-family, Boeing 737/777/787/747 and ATR72 aircraft and engines including the V2500, LEAP-1A, CFM56-5B, GE and JT8D. The Government of India has been in the process of divesting AIESL, inviting expressions of interest for its privatisation. AIESL's military-aerospace relevance lies in its status as India's largest strategic MRO PSU and national deep-maintenance capacity; however, primary public evidence of dedicated military-aircraft MRO work is limited, so this entry is tiered B on its documented civil heavy-MRO footprint and government-owned strategic status.

deployments_procurement.summary: AIESL's role is as a service provider rather than a procurement contractor. It is Air India's preferred MRO partner and the country's largest heavy-maintenance provider, operating hangars and line stations nationwide. The dominant strategic storyline in the review period is its pending privatisation by the Government of India.

import_dependencies.summary: As an MRO, AIESL depends structurally on foreign airframe and engine OEMs for spare parts, rotables, engines, tooling and licensed maintenance data and repair schemes. Its heavy-maintenance and engine-overhaul capabilities are performed in India but under OEM (Airbus, Boeing, ATR, CFM, IAE, GE, Pratt & Whitney) approvals and using imported components.

faq.question: What is AIESL and who owns it?
faq.answer: AI Engineering Services Limited (formerly Air India Engineering Services Limited) is India's largest aircraft MRO organisation and the former engineering arm of Air India. When Air India was privatised and sold to the Tata Group, AIESL was retained by the Government of India and remains a wholly government-owned PSU under the Ministry of Civil Aviation. It is headquartered at the Safdarjung Airport Complex in New Delhi.

faq.question: What can AIESL do and what is its future?
faq.answer: AIESL performs base/heavy checks, engine overhaul, component overhaul, landing-gear and wheels-and-brakes servicing, NDT and battery services across A320, B737/777/787/747 and ATR72 aircraft and engines such as the V2500, LEAP-1A and CFM56-5B, with hangars at six cities, 50+ line stations and 16 FAA/EASA/DGCA approvals. The Government of India has been in the process of divesting/privatising AIESL, and its ownership and mandate after privatisation remain to be settled.
